title: How to Quote, Invoice, and Get Paid with Topline Pro
summary: Learn how to save your rates, create and send quotes, turn jobs into invoices, collect card or ACH payments, and automate follow-up with Topline Pro.
body_markdown:
## Key Takeaways


- Topline Pro keeps **every step from quote to paid invoice in one app** , with **Sidekick** applying your saved rates and handling follow-up.
- **Base rates** let you set labor rates, material costs, and upcharge rules once, then apply them to every quote and invoice. **(Just tell Sidekick!)**
- **Line-item grouping** lets you bundle crew, equipment, and materials you often use together so you can **add them to a quote in one step.**
- **Pricing visibility** lets you give the homeowner a simple, readable bill, while you still see the full breakdown.
- **Recurring invoices** let you bill repeat customers on a schedule (and Sidekick reminds you when one is due).


Topline Pro uses automation to help you fire off quotes and invoices, and follow up when things go unpaid. That leads to faster payment and a lot of saved time for your business.


Most home service pros can eyeball a job and know how much it’s going to cost because they’ve done similar work before. The headache only happens when you have to rebuild that quote line by line every time. Worse, when it’s time to invoice, you end up typing all that information over again.


Topline Pro cuts all that work. Tell Sidekick, Topline Pro’s proprietary AI, how you price jobs. After that, it pulls those rates and plugs them into your quotes and invoices for you automatically.


## What’s new in quoting and invoicing


Topline Pro’s October 2026 release adds more of the pricing controls pros like you told us they needed to rely on our app for everyday quoting and invoicing.


The big additions are:


- **Base rates:** Save labor and material rates, along with the rules you use to adjust those rates (like charging a premium for your most experienced hands).
- **Line-item grouping:** Bundle crew members, equipment, materials, and other line items that you regularly use together for certain types of jobs. For example, if you know you need to account for travel time and a bigger lawnmower to landscape a house in the posh subdivision at the edge of town, group those items together.
- **Pricing visibility:** Control how much line-item detail homeowners see on invoices. Clients generally don’t need to see staff names and equipment models on their invoice.
- **Recurring invoices:** Automatically bill repeat customers on a schedule, or let Sidekick remind you when it’s time to send one.


These features help get pricing knowledge out of your head and into the app so Sidekick can do the work for you.


## Go from quote to paid invoice in eight steps


Topline Pro helps you go from quote to paid more quickly because it keeps all those steps in one tool and then automates most of the process. If you’re using the Topline Pro app already, all you need to do is update the mobile app. If you’re new to Topline Pro, you can[download it here](https://www.toplinepro.com/signup) to try it for free.


### 1. Set up payments and tell Sidekick your rates (labor, materials, upcharges)


Before you send your next invoice, connect your Stripe account in Topline Pro so you can accept card and ACH payments. There’s a to-do list underneath the Sidekick app on the home screen that will let you know if this step isn’t done yet.


Then, start giving Sidekick the rates and pricing rules you use every day. You can do this by voice or text, whichever is more comfortable.


Be sure to describe things like:


- Labor rates
- Material costs
- Minimums
- Upcharges


For example, say your base labor rate is $20 an hour. But if Sarah, who is highly skilled, is working the job, you charge 10% more. It’s 30% more if she works a holiday to knock out a rush job.


Just describe rules like that to Sidekick, and it applies them for you.


### 2. Group line items for jobs you quote often


Say you run a landscaping company and your crews regularly drive as much as two hours to reach properties in far-flung, high-dollar neighborhoods. These jobs tend to be larger properties and require certain, more experienced crew members, along with heavier equipment.


Instead of adding those upcharges one at a time every time you quote a job out there, you can save those items as a group. The next time a job comes in from that neighborhood, just apply the group to the quote.


### 3. Create a quote


Create a quote by explaining the job to Sidekick by either text or voice. Sidekick finds the customer’s contact information, builds the quote, and shows it to you for your review. It only takes about 90 seconds.


### 4. Choose what the homeowner sees


Sidekick understands that while you need to see a detailed price breakdown, your client doesn’t need all the math.


For example, say you’ve got a hardscaping job that you’re quoting. You need to see labor rates, equipment costs, materials, and disposal fees. On the client side, Sidekick can simplify all that information into a descriptive but concise line like “Hardscaping, front of house – $4,500.”


A homeowner usually cares about what work you’re doing and what it costs, not which employee worked which hours or what every individual material cost. Pricing visibility lets you keep the detail you need to run the job while giving the customer a clear, easy-to-read bill.


### 5. Send it for signature


Once the quote Sidekick gives you looks right, send it to your prospective client by text or email along with a personal note.


On their end, the homeowner gets a mobile-friendly link that opens to a page with your logo, line items, any necessary deposits or milestones, and other contract terms. They can accept it right from the page with a time-stamped e-signature.


The app notifies you both when the homeowner opens the quote and when they accept it. If they don’t respond, Sidekick can handle follow-up communications for you automatically.


### 6. Turn the quote into an invoice once the job is done


Once the work is done, all you have to do to generate the invoice is tell Sidekick anything that changed about the job. Say your tech worked eight hours instead of six, or had to buy an additional part to complete the work. Let Sidekick know, and it will make those adjustments before spitting out an invoice for your review.


### 7. Set up recurring invoices for repeat jobs


For repeat jobs where the price stays the same, like monthly lawn treatment or biweekly housecleaning services, you can have Sidekick send invoices on a regular schedule. Or, if you’d rather send them yourself, Sidekick can remind you later.


### 8. Get paid by card or ACH, with automatic follow-up on unpaid invoices


Homeowners can pay invoices online by card or ACH. Topline Pro keeps those payments tied to the invoice so you can see right in your app whether a customer has paid. Like with quotes, Sidekick notifies you when a customer opens their invoice and again when they pay it.


If a customer pays by cash or check, simply mark the invoice paid in the app.


Sidekick can automatically follow up on unpaid invoices, so you don’t have to remember to bug clients by text or email.
